n: The Ziphites again betray David's hiding place to Saul — despite Saul's earlier tearful promise at En-gedi.
Saul sets out again with three thousand elite soldiers to hunt David in the wilderness of Ziph. His repentance in chapter 24 did not last.
Saul camps by the road on the hill of Hachilah. David, hiding in the wilderness, sees that Saul has come after him.
David sends scouts and confirms that Saul has truly arrived.
David goes near Saul's camp and observes where Saul and his commander Abner are sleeping, with the army camped in a circle around them.

f.g: the camp's inner circle, perhaps ringed by wagons

n: David asks who will sneak into the camp with him. Abishai, David's nephew and Joab's brother, volunteers. Ahimelech the Hittite shows David had foreigners among his loyal men.

f.g: Zeruiah was David's sister; her sons Joab, Abishai, and Asahel became David's fierce commanders.

n: At night David and Abishai find Saul asleep in the center of camp, his spear stuck in the ground by his head — a symbol of his royal authority — with Abner and the troops around him.
Abishai urges David to let him pin Saul to the ground with one thrust of the spear — God has delivered him, he argues.

f.w: I will not smite him the second time

n: David forbids it: no one can harm the Lord's anointed and remain guiltless. David honors God's choice even when that person is his enemy.
David trusts that the Lord will deal with Saul in His own way — by striking him, by natural death, or in battle. Waiting on God's timing takes great faith.

f.w: his day shall come to die

n: David says the Lord forbid that he harm Saul, but tells Abishai to take Saul's spear and water jug as proof.
They take the spear and jug and leave unseen. No one wakes, because the Lord had put the whole camp into a deep sleep.

f.w: a deep sleep from the LORD

n: David crosses to the top of a hill far away, keeping a safe distance between himself and the camp.
David shouts to the army and taunts Abner: aren't you going to answer? Abner wakes and demands to know who is shouting at the king.
David mocks Abner: aren't you Israel's greatest warrior? Why didn't you guard the king? Someone came to kill him!
David declares that Abner and his men deserve death for failing to protect the Lord's anointed. As proof, he asks where the king's spear and water jug are.
Saul recognizes David's voice and calls him “my son David,” as at En-gedi. David answers respectfully.

f.w: Is this thy voice, my son David?

n: David asks again why Saul pursues him. What has he done wrong?

David reasons: if the Lord stirred Saul against him, let an offering make it right. But if men did it, may they be cursed — they have driven David from the Lord's land, as if telling him to go serve other gods.

f.g: Let an offering appease God's anger, if David has sinned.
the land of Israel and its worship

n: David asks that his blood not be spilled far from the Lord's presence. Why would the king hunt a flea, as one hunts a partridge in the mountains?

f.g: Partridges were hunted by being chased until exhausted — a picture of David's endless flight. The Hebrew name also sounds like “the caller,” as David is calling out.

n: Saul confesses, “I have sinned... I have played the fool.” He promises not to harm David again because David valued his life. Sadly, these words won't change his heart.
David tells Saul to send a young man to retrieve the king's spear. He doesn't return it personally, perhaps not trusting Saul's promise.
David expresses faith that the Lord rewards each person for righteousness and faithfulness. He spared Saul though God put him in his power.

f.w: The LORD render to every man his righteousness

n: David prays that as he valued Saul's life, the Lord will value his life and deliver him from all trouble. He looks to God, not Saul, for safety.

f.w: deliver me out of all tribulation

n: Saul blesses David and predicts that David will do great things and succeed. They part ways. This is the last time Saul and David meet.

f.w: thou shalt both do great things
